newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-MEXICO'S MORELIA BEGIN BIZARRE BATTLE WITH 3-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO'S MORELIA BEGIN BIZARRE BATTLE WITH 3-0 WIN.

text.p: Mexican soccer club Morelia are likely to be simultaneously fighting for the title and trying to avoid relegation in the national championship tournament which began on Sunday.

Morelia, who had been one of the top teams in the opening tourney of the 1997 season, confirmed that they are likely to be among the title contenders again as they hammered Toros Neza 3-0 on the first day of the year's second and final tournament.

But even if they win the title they could be condemned to the second division next year as relegation is decided on average points per game over the previous three years, a criterion in which Morelia are struggling.
Goals by Chilean Marco Figueroa, Brazilian Claudinho and local player Daniel Deeke gave Morelia an ideal start.
Champions Guadalajara, who have stuck to their tradition of using only Mexican players in a league awash with foreign stars, began the defence of their crown with a 2-1 win over Atletico Celaya.
